report:
PASS applies only to the declared limited A–I theorem. The author argument, the complete A–H reconstruction, and the separate I reconstruction establish its assertions under the stated conventions. The historical original-task INCONCLUSIVE and both unrestricted candidate=false results remain unchanged. Audit flags, hashes, numerical diagnostics, and earlier verdicts were not used as mathematical premises.

A is correct. Writing β=αT^(α−1), direct differentiation gives A′=p+(1−p)β and A″=p(1−p)(1−β)+α(1−α)(1−p)²T^(α−2). Thus 0<A′<1, A″>0, and A″≤Bα:=1/4+α(1−α). The left asymptotics give the genuine sublogarithmic pole and tangent intercept tending to −∞. At the right end, A−x=(1−α)e^(−x)+O(e^(−2x)), and the tangent intercept tends to zero. The specified infinity expression is smooth in the projective function σ=|Z₀|²/Σᵢ≥1|Zᵢ|². Canonical extension is valid at both ends. In fact κ+Dψ≥(1−α)κ. Both κ and H satisfy the task’s bigness definition with potential zero.

B retains every competitor. The family is nonempty, locally uniformly upper bounded, and invariant under U(k); its regularized supremum remains below the usc obstacle, including at the pole. Its radial total profile is convex by complex-line restriction. Conversely, the finite convex minorant C lies between A±‖F‖∞, has slopes in [0,1] and limiting slopes 0 and 1, and produces a genuine admissible global potential. The radial Hessian and canonical extensions establish this converse. These inequalities force the exact full-envelope formula and ordinary equivalence to ψ; no radial restriction of the original competitor family is imposed.

C–D hold for arbitrary C² compact obstacles, including accumulating free components. Chord replacement proves affineness on every gap component. At contact, C′₋≥g′≥C′₊ and convexity force equality. Using the first and last contacts in any interval gives the asserted Lipschitz bound for C′, without an assumption about the number of gaps. The left tangent test gives exact agreement C=A near the pole. If L=inf(g−x) is attained, the touching slope-one minorant and C′≤1 force C=x+L on the entire subsequent ray. Negative L is necessarily attained. Otherwise L=0 is unattained, and the right tangent test gives C=A eventually. These exhaust the alternatives. The residual is defined off the pole and extended by its actual nearby zero value. On an annulus x≥a₀ its gradient is bounded by 2e^(−a₀/2), and its Hessian by [4(QF+Bα)+2]e^(−a₀), where QF=sup max(g″,0). The end formulas establish global C¹,¹ residual regularity and smoothness near infinity.

E–F have the correct normalization. The smooth radial determinant is k!π^(−k)(C′)^(k−1)C″r^(−k) times Euclidean volume. Bounded decreasing approximation identifies this with the actual local product, whose radial pushforward is d(C′ᵏ). Consequently every stated annular mass formula holds and radial boundary atoms vanish. Strict-superlevel truncations discard the pole; smoothness at infinity excludes hyperplane mass. The end slopes give total mass one. Affine gaps have zero top density and rank k−1 when their slope is positive. The negative bump inequality really forces L<0 and a strict open free right tail. Translating competitors proves constant-one C⁰ stability, including the canonically extended residual values.

G is valid for every stated Hermitian factor and all product competitors. Locally, adding a closed horizontal κ-potential and a vertical quadratic dominating h₀ makes a competitor genuinely psh. Canonical restriction to each horizontal slice is psh or identically −∞; subtracting the correction gives exactly κ+D_zv≥0. Connectedness supplies the global slice alternative. Every slice is therefore below the base envelope, while the base envelope lifts as an admissible competitor. The convolution slicing proof also passes its uniform background error to zero correctly. At bounded pullback truncations, dimensional vanishing leaves precisely the binomial tensor term. Strict-superlevel restrictions then give the claimed finite extended measure and mass. This calculation requires no general BMP-dependent unbounded-product theorem. For stretching, t=1 uses a₁=E_F^H; every real t>1 uses a_t=ψ−t‖F‖∞. Both satisfy the actual defining inequality with canonical pole values. The residual estimates pull back to each fixed product atlas.

H checks directly: h₀=iΣdζⱼ∧dζ̄ⱼ/(2π|ζ|²), so it is positive and invariant under the deck transformation. Also dh₀=−ds∧Ds≠0. The quotient is compact and diffeomorphic to S³×S¹. Independently of the Betti-number argument, the descended exact semipositive rank-one form Ds would have strictly positive integral against a Kähler form, contradicting Stokes. Thus both the Hopf surface and the fourfold product are non-Kähler. The supplementary normalization V₀=4 and fourfold representative mass 24 is correct. No lower-mass property follows from this calculation or is needed.

I is established uniformly through moving infinity contact. Choose a common t₋<min(a,0) satisfying A(t₋)+A′(t₋)(b−t₋)≤A(a)−M. Every residual vanishes for x≤t₋. Set W=2Bα+M; the uniform profile bounds are |R_F|≤M, |R_F′|≤1, and |R_F″|≤W almost everywhere. On x>b, strict convexity of A rules out a free component wholly contained in that region. The possibilities are no gap, one tangent segment ending at a finite contact, or an affine slope-one tail.

For B(σ)=log(1+σ)+1−(1+log(1+σ))^α, differentiation gives 0<B′≤1, −1/(1+σ)²≤B″<0, and σ|B″|≤1/4. Moreover σB′ is increasing. The finite-contact tangent formula and affine-tail formula therefore give |R_σ|≤1 and σ|R_σσ|≤5/4 in every alternative, independently of the contact radius. In the supplied projective charts σ=|τ|²/S, |Dσ|²≤8σ and ‖D²σ‖≤12. Hence ‖D²R_F‖≤22 near infinity. The normal gradient is bounded by 2|τ|, the tangential gradient by σ, and |R_F−R_∞|≤|τ|². These establish actual differentiability and a uniform Lipschitz gradient across the hyperplane. In the affine-tail alternative its normal Hessian there is −2(1−α)S^(−1)I₂; the other blocks vanish. In the unchanged-tail alternative all blocks vanish. All derivatives vanish on the common pole neighborhood.

The explicit chart constants are valid: U=max(2e^(−t₋/2),√(4e^b+1),4√2), H=max((4W+2)e^(−t₋),W(4e^b+1)+2max(e^b,1),22), and K=M+U+H. The continuous gradient and almost-everywhere Hessian bound imply the asserted Lipschitz bound on the convex chart domains. For Z=R_F−R_G, value stability gives ‖Z‖∞≤δ. Taylor increments on the nested charts give ‖DZ‖∞≤A*√δ, where A*=8+H/4. Interpolating min(2A*√δ,2H|x−y|) proves the stated C¹,γ estimate, with Kγ=1+A*+(2A*)^(1−γ)(2H)^γ. The δ=0 case follows from value stability. The changing-contact bump family is also proved: its critical parameter lies in (0,1), and uniform value stability forces its finite right contacts to escape to infinity from below. Thus the difficult family quantifier is genuinely covered. No C¹,¹ convergence is inferred.

The credited radial-density manuscript was checked as background. Its positive cumulative-flux inverse remains smooth across density zeros. The central error integral yields the displayed residual derivative bounds and crossing thresholds; its flat-error and compensated zero-annulus constructions are valid. Its zero-lower-mass product assertion remains conditional on the expressly stated factor hypothesis. That implication supplies neither an unconditional factor existence claim nor a lower-mass assertion for H. The reference, radial flux mechanism, and earlier density criteria therefore retain their existing credit.

The primary applications were reopened in [Demailly](https://people.math.harvard.edu/~demarco/Math274/Demailly_ComplexAnalyticDiffGeom.pdf), [Bedford–Taylor](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~ebedford/PapersForM655/BTNewCapacity.pdf), [BGL](https://arxiv.org/html/2406.01090v1), and [BEGZ](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0812.3674v2). The applications respect their local boundedness, closedness, positivity, and canonical-representative requirements. BGL’s general Section 2.2 extension assumes BMP and is not used on arbitrary Y. Task passages below record granted conventions rather than additional external assumptions.

The literature comparison is accurate for Ahn’s continuity theorem in both cited editions, [v2](https://arxiv.org/html/2604.01885v2) and [v3](https://arxiv.org/html/2604.01885v3), [Ahn’s Hölder theorem](https://arxiv.org/html/2604.01887v3), and [Nguyen](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2305.04171). Their weights are finite. Ahn’s operator normalization is 4π times D; these results are used for comparison, not to prove A–I. Here K=X satisfies capacity density: the constant test potential gives a uniform lower bound cr^(2N) on coordinate balls. The distinction is the singular weight, retained ordinary type, and quantified residual. It is not a capacity-density-failure example or a priority claim.

Harmless corrections are explicit. R is a smooth projective function, not a coordinate. End slopes 0 and 1 refer to the maximal C with its sandwich bounds, not arbitrary affine minorants. At t=1 the zero-coefficient pole term must be omitted; the current separate witness does so. The supplied purported Hodge excerpt actually displays Section VI.6; the required VI.8.12 passage was independently located. Ahn’s printed Hölder proof reverses the inequality δ^s≤δ for 0<s<1; shrinking the small-radius constant so δ₀^s≤min(δ₁,r₂) preserves its estimate and exponent. None requires a substantive repair of A–I.

The theorem answers a specific ordinary everywhere singular-obstacle problem and its fixed-support stability family. Arbitrary prescribed equation types and densities, general compact obstacle sets, and ideal-ordered quasi-everywhere weighted extremals remain unresolved. The computed masses are actual representative masses; lower and upper singularity-volume extrema remain distinct.

passages.statement: For a locally uniformly upper-bounded family of plurisubharmonic functions on a complex domain, the usc regularization of its supremum is plurisubharmonic and agrees almost everywhere with the supremum. Demailly, I.5.7.

A distribution with positive complex Hessian has a unique locally integrable plurisubharmonic representative. Fixed nonnegative smooth radial mollifications of a plurisubharmonic function nontrivial on each component decrease pointwise to it as their radii decrease, and are smooth plurisubharmonic on smaller domains. Decreasing plurisubharmonic sequences have plurisubharmonic limits, allowing −∞. Demailly, I.5.4–5.5 and I.5.8.

passages.quote: All potentials are genuine canonical quasi-psh representatives, with pole values included.

passages.statement: Holomorphic pullback preserves plurisubharmonicity, allowing an identically −∞ restriction on a connected component. Demailly, I.5.11.
A plurisubharmonic function extends uniquely across a closed pluripolar subset of a complex manifold if it is locally bounded above near that subset. Demailly, I.5.24.

Locally bounded plurisubharmonic functions on complex domains have symmetric multilinear Bedford–Taylor wedge products that are positive closed currents. If every input sequence decreases pointwise to a locally bounded plurisubharmonic limit, the products converge weakly to the product of those limits. Bedford–Taylor, A new capacity for plurisubharmonic functions, Theorem 2.1 and Corollary 2.2.
passages.quote: where the limit is in the weak topology

passages.statement: On a compact complex n-fold, for 1≤p≤n, smooth real (1,1)-forms θ_i and bounded quasi-psh functions u_i define smooth-background-corrected products of T_i=θ_i+ddᶜu_i by multilinear expansion. These products depend only on T_i, are symmetric, multilinear, non-pluripolar and plurifine-local, and are positive when every T_i is positive. Compatible restricted products exist on compact subsets where the potentials are bounded. These assertions require no bounded mass property. Boucksom–Guedj–Lu, Section 2.1, Proposition 2.1.
passages.quote: acting on tuples of quasi-psh functions bounded on $K$ is local in the plurifine topology.

passages.quote: Extended products are non-pluripolar products with smooth-background corrections.

passages.statement: Every odd Betti number of a compact Kähler manifold is even. Demailly, VI.8.12.

Using ddᶜ=2i∂∂̄, let (X,ω) be a compact Hermitian manifold, K⊂X a compact non-pluripolar set, and V_{K,w}=sup{u∈PSH(X,ω):u≤w on K}, with V_K=V_{K,0}. If w:X→ℝ is continuous and V_K is continuous, then V_{K,w} is continuous. Ahn, arXiv:2604.01885v2 and v3, Theorem 1.4(ii).
passages.quote: If $\phi:X\to\mathbb{R}$ is continuous and $V_{K}$ is continuous, then $V_{K,\phi}$ is continuous.

Let (X,ω) be a compact Kähler manifold and K⊂X a compact non-pluripolar set. For V_{K,w}=sup{u∈PSH(X,ω):u≤w on K}, a finite continuous weight w:X→ℝ and continuity of V_{K,0} imply continuity of V_{K,w}. Nguyen, Regularity of the Siciak-Zaharjuta extremal function on compact Kähler manifolds, Theorem 1.1(b).
passages.quote: If VK is continuous, then VK,φ is continuous.

passages.statement: For 1≤p≤n, closed positive (1,1)-currents on a compact Kähler n-fold have well-defined non-pluripolar products with locally finite mass. The construction is plurifine-local, puts no mass on pluripolar sets, and locally uses increasing strict-superlevel restrictions of bounded plurisubharmonic truncation products. Boucksom–Eyssidieux–Guedj–Zeriahi, arXiv:0812.3674v2, Section 1.2 and Proposition 1.6.
